questions.stem: Why do simple covalent substances have low boiling points?

options.text: The covalent bonds within molecules are weak
The intermolecular forces between molecules are weak and require little energy to overcome
The molecules are very heavy and sink to the bottom
The atoms inside the molecules break apart easily

questions.explanation: Simple covalent substances have low boiling points because the intermolecular forces between molecules are weak and require little energy to overcome. The covalent bonds within the molecules are strong and do NOT break during boiling - only the weak forces between molecules are overcome.

questions.stem: Why do simple covalent substances not conduct electricity?

options.text: They have very strong covalent bonds
They are always gases at room temperature
They have no free charged particles such as ions or delocalised electrons
Their molecules are too small to carry a current

questions.explanation: Simple covalent substances do not conduct electricity because they have no free charged particles. Their molecules are electrically neutral (no ions), and all their electrons are used in covalent bonds (no delocalised electrons). Even when melted, they remain as neutral molecules.
